Meeting Schedule

The regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month,

  1
 closed session business will usually commence at 5:30 p.m., when scheduled, and general business
session will commence at 6:30 p.m.

Brown Act

Agendas are drafted to accurately state what the legislative body is being asked to consider. The
legislative body can take action on "all items" listed on the agenda and be in compliance with the open
meeting laws. Under the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the
agenda, or unless certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The governing body may direct
staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for consideration at a future meeting.

City's Vision Statement

We envision a thriving, safe and inclusive community where everyone has the opportunity to access
exceptional services, education and support to be resilient and live full, vibrant lives.

Public Communications

Public Comments on agenda items are limited to three (3) minutes. All comments are to be addressed
directly to the Agency Members not to the members of the public.

Emails for public comment received prior to 4:00 pm on the day of the Council Meeting will be
summarized by the City Clerk, not read in its entirety. A copy of the email will be provided to the City
Council and will also be available at the City Clerk's Office for public review. A copy of each email will be
recorded for public record and noted on the official minutes of tonight's meeting.

GENERAL NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC

The City Council adopted new rules relating to the conduct of the public meetings, proceedings, and
business in the City of South Gate on July 12, 2022, (Resolution 2022-38-CC) and go into effect on
August 1, 2022. Resolution #2022-38-CC is available at the City Clerk’s Office.

MEETING SCHEDULE

Regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month, closed
session meetings will commence at 5:30 p.m. unless posted otherwise on its agenda. The regular City
Council meetings will commence at 6:30 p.m. Agendas are available at the following locations: City Clerk
Office, Public Notice Boards at City Hall, and on the City’s web page at https://www.cityofsouthgate.org

The Public can sign up to receive automatic notices of postings of agendas for the City Council or any
other Commission or Board of the City of South Gate. Visit the City webpage and click on the Agenda &
Minutes icon. That will take you the page where an individual can enter their email in the “Email
Updates” box to register.

PUBLIC COMMENT/PARTICIPATION

Any person may request to address a legislative body during a public meeting. The Presiding Officer will
call upon those present in the Council Chambers.

Speakers are limited to three (3) minutes on any item listed on the agenda, including public hearings.
Under Comments from the Audience portion, speakers are also limited to a single three (3) minutes time
limit. Comments from the Audience is initially limited to 45 minutes at each meeting. Any speaker still
wishing to speak, that did not speak, will have an addition Comments from the Audience opportunity after
the last business item is finished. The Presiding Officer may extend the time limit as long as there is no
objection from the City Council as a body.

To ensure that the public is able to participate, the City provides the opportunity to submit their

  7
 comments in person, email, mail. Methods of participation may be subject to change during other such
times when a State of Emergency, Health Order or State Executive Order limits in-person participation.

CURFEW

In absence of a motion duly adopted by majority vote of the City Council, the Presiding Officer may
adjourn the City Council meetings at 10:30 p.m. The Presiding Officer may ask the City Council if any
agenda items listed should be continued or dealt with during the meeting. For those items to be
continued, the City Council can direct the item be placed on the next City Council agenda or the current
meeting may be adjourned to a time certain at which time the meeting shall be reconvened as an
Adjourned Regular Meeting of the City Council and action upon the published agenda continued.

STAFF REPORTS

As a general rule, staff reports. or other written documentation are prepared/organized with respect to
each item of business listed on the agenda. Meeting agendas and staff reports are available at least 72-
hours prior to the scheduled regular City Council meeting and a minimum of 24-hours prior to a Special
City Council meeting. There are times when the City Council receives written material. revised material
after the posting of agendas, these materials are become a public record and will be available for public
view within 72-hours after the meeting in which they were received. Those materials and any other public
document can be inspected in the City Clerk's Office located at 8650 California Avenue, South Gate.

SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS

In compliance with the American with Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in the
City Council Meetings, please contact the Office of the City Clerk. Notification 48 hours prior to the City
Council Meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to assure accessibility. For
further information, please contact the Office of the City Clerk at (323) 563-9510 or via email at
yglaze@sogate.org.

 BACKGROUND:

Live Entertainment
The applicant requests approval to provide live entertairu'nent at the Project Site. Live entertainment
will be limited to musical performances of no more than four (4) performers at atime. Performances
will take place in the outdoor stage area adjacent to the ground-floor  bar.

Schedule of Entertainment:
  *  : Friday,  Saturday, and Sunday
  *  Times: 12:00 PM-10:00  PM

Entertainment will be oriented inward toward the courtyard to minimize sound transmission to
surrounding properties. All performances will comply with city noise standards and operational
conditions.

Site History  and Environmental  Setting
The Project Site consists of three lots: one developed lot and two vacant lots. The developed lot
(3703 Tweedy Boulevard) at the northeastern corner of Tweedy Boulevard and San Carlos Avenue
has a one-story, 2,392 SF commercial building constructed in the 1950s. It was formerly used as a
dental/medical office, but the building is now vacant. Based on aerial photographs, the two vacant
lots located east of the commercial building have been vacant for over 30 years. There are no
building permits on file showing that the lots were ever developed.

The entire site is flat with paved sidewalks, stable valley soils, and surrounded by low-rise
commercial storefronts and nearby residences. Vegetation is minimal, limited to a few street trees
along the public sidewalks and ornamental plants onsite. There are no sensitive habitats or protected
species in the area. Wildlife consists of cornrnon urban birds and small mammals. There are no
known historical, cultural, or scenic designations on the property.

The property is part of the Tweedy Mile corridor and is required to have an active retail frontage
that encourages pedestrian activity. Properties along Tweedy Boulevard adjacent to the subject site
are developed with commercial uses. Residential uses are located to the north along San Carlos
Avenue.

  alley and public parking to the north. Table 1 provides a summary of the lot dimensions and

History  of Land  Use and Zoning  of Subject  Property
Inl950, the property at 3703 Tweedy Boulevard was developed as amedical building. A 14-foot by
28-foot carport was built in the rear of the building. There are no permits for the two vacant lots to
the east; however, a history of code violations  has occurred over the decades, including overgrown
vegetation,  weeds,  trash, debris,  and parking  on an unimproved  area. Violations  of graffiti  have also
been reported  on the existing  building.

In 2019, the City  adopted  the Tweedy  Boulevard  Specific  Plan. The zoning  for the subject  property
and adjacent  properties  along  Tweedy  Boulevard  was changed  from  Restricted  Commercial  (C-2)
to Tweedy  Mixed  Use-2  (TMU2).  Properties  to the west across San Carlos  Avenue  were changed  to
Tweedy  Mixed  Use-l  (TMUI).  An  "Active  Retail  Frontage"  corridor  was  established  from
Elizabeth  Avenue  to the west to Bowman  Avenue  to the east, which  includes  the subject  property.

Planning  Commission  Meeting
On October  21, 2025, the Planning  Commission  conducted  a public  hearing  on a Conditional  Use
Permit  (CUP No. 25-04)  and a Site Plan Review  (PL No. 25-0312)  to consider  development  of an
open-air  food hall with  a central  outdoor  plaza,  7,718  square  feet of building  area, eight  restaurant
vendor  spaces, live entertainment,  landscaping,  signage,  and other improvements.  Two  vendors  will
be selling  alcohol  under a Type 47 license  ("On-Sale  General  Eating  Place")  issued by the California
Department  of Alcoholic  Beverage  Control  (ABC).

The  applicant  spoke  on behalf  of the project,  and 10 other  speakers  from  the public  provided
testimony.  All  the speakers  were  in support  of the project.  One resident  asked  about  the type  of
entertainment  and how the owner  would  control  the venues to ensure a family-friendly  environment.

  4

  12
 The Planning  Commission  asked questions  of the applicant  and staff and deliberated  on the item.  At
the conclusion of the public  hearing,  the Commission  voted  unanimously,  5-0, to approve  CUP No.
25-04 and PL No. 25-0312.

ANALYSIS:

Tweedy  Boulevard  Specific  Plan (TBSP)  Requirements  for a CUP:  Pursuant  to TBSP  Table  4-2,
"Live  Entertainment"  requires  a Conditional  Use Permit  (CUP).  A CUP is subject  to the procedures
in SGMC  Section  11.51.030  (Permits  and Procedures,  Review  Types  and Responsibilities)  and
Chapter  11.52 (Conditional  Use Permit).  Under  SGMC  Table  11.51-1,  a CUP for live entertainment
requires  approval by the City Council.

Required  Findings  for a CUP:  Pursuant  to SGMC  Section  11.52.030,  before  a CUP may be granted,
the City  Council  shall make all the following  findings,  as applicable  to the property:

  A.  Approval  of the CUP is consistent  with  and will  not adversely  affect  the intent  and purpose
  of this title  or the city's  General  Plan.

  B.  ThedesignanddevelopmentofthelanduseandconditionsoftheCUParecompatiblewith
  the existing  and future  land uses of the applicable  zone.

  C.  Approval  of the CUP would  not result  in detrimental  impacts  to adjacent  properties  or to
  the character  or function  of the neighborhood.

The proposed  Resolution  supports  the findings  required  under  Section  11.52.030.

Issues  of Concern

Parkiy
The project  site is within  the Active  Retail  Frontage  district  commonly  known  as "Tweedy  Mile."
Whereas  the City's  Zoning  Code provides  for parking  requirements  based  on land use types,  the
TBSP  embraces  the concept  of shared  parking,  where  parking  supplies  are available  to all users,
rather than being  limited  to a single  land use or building  (TBSP  Chapter  5 - Mobility  and Parking).
The overall  parking  strategy  for Tweedy  Mile  is to provide  sufficient  parking  to ensure  economic
viability  and success of commercial  uses. The listed parking  strategies  in the TBSP  include  the "Park
Once"  concept  and program,  which  "is  intended  to consolidate  parking  resources,  relieve  individual
properties  of providing  potentially  duplicative  parking,  reduce  individual  vehicle  trips,  and group
parking  facilities  in strategically  dispersed  locations  to encourage  walking  between  destinations."

Per SGMC  Section  11.33.040,  a food use with  7,718  square feet of building  area would  be required
to provide  115 onsite parking  spaces. This is based on a factor  of 40 spaces for the first 4,000 square
feet, plus 1 space for every  50 square feet over 4,000  square feet. However,  per Assembly  Bill  2097
(AB  2097)  cities are prohibited  from imposing  a minimum  automobile  parking  requirement  on most
development  projects  located  within  a half-mile  radius  of a major  transit  stop. Tweedy  Boulevard  is
a major  commercial  and mixed-use  corridor  with  adequate  public  transit.  Furthermore,  the TBSP
encourages  a walkable  environment  where  visitors  can visit  multiple  destinations  and "park  once."

  5

  13
 This provides  an opportunity  for revised  parking  standards  along Tweedy  Mile.  TBSP  indicates  there
is a considerable  amount  of parking  supply  in the Specific  Plan  area, including  2,865  off-street
parking  spaces (78%  privately  owned;  22% owned  by the City).  Over  80% of the off-street  supply,
or 2,345  spaces, are located  in Tweedy  Mile  where  the project  site is located.  The off-street  supply
comprises  635 spaces in City-owned  lots and 1,710  spaces in private  lots.

In the Park Once Program  Area,  the parking  requirements  may be met within  1,300  feet (!/l mile)  of
a specific  land use. The applicant  has demonstrated  in Attachment  2 that there are 144 public  parking
spaces  within  O.15 miles  of the project  site. This  does not include  on-street  parking  and private
parking  lots.  The  public  parking  available  on City-owned  lots  and public  streets  is more  than
adequate  to meet the parking  spaces otherwise  required  by Code. Furthermore,  as mentioned  earlier,
the applicant  is exploring  opportunities  with  nearby  properties  for shared parking  on private  parking
lots. A shared parking  agreement  would  prevent  towing  of vehicles  belonging  to food hall customers
if parked  in a private  lot in the event the owner  of the private  lot decides  to enforce  parking  rules.

Noise
Those  most impacted  are the residents  north  of the project  site along  San Carlos  Avenue.  Although
there is an alley  and public  parking  lot between  the project  site and adjacent  residences,  the closest
distance  is only about 60 feet building  to building.  As such, a noise study has been prepared  for City
Council's  consideration  and is included  as Attachment  D. Conditions  of approval  have been included
in the Resolution  to mitigate  noise impacts,  which  are based on the noise study's  recommendations.

The conditions  require  the following:

  *  Reduced  volume  for speakers  located  in the rear terrace  and upper  lounge.
  *  Noise  barriers:
  ffl  10-foot-highbarrierforentrancealongrearalley
  ffl  10-foot-high  barrier  in rear lounge
  ffl  7-foot-high  barrier  for play area
  *  Noise  restrictions  a:[ter 10 p.m.  in rear areas

EXECUTIVE  SUMMARY

AcousticsGroup, Inc., (AGI) was retainedto conducta noise study for The Place @
Tweedy  Project  in South Gate, CA.  AGI has reviewed  the City of South Gate Noise
Standards,  conducted  noise measurements,  analyzed  the noise levels from future noise
sources at the site, assessed the impact of the future noise to determine compliance  with
the Exterior Noise Standards, and recommended  noise control measures.

The Place @ Tweedy proposes an open-air Outdoor food hall with a central outdoor plaza
providing live entertainment. Two operating cases were evaluated:  Case I (Typica[
Operations  Noise (without live entertainment  10AM to 11PM)  and Case 2 (Typical
Operations  Noise with Live music entertainment  12PM to 9PM).

For Case 1, the future noise level without noise control would be 55.4, 44.7, and 50.4 dBA
at the residences  to the north (ST1 ), south (ST2), and northwest  (ST3), respectively.  The
operations  noise at the nearest residential  receptors  to north (ST1 ) and northwest  (ST3)
would  exceed  the City of South  Gate  Daytime  Noise  Standard  of 50 dBA. At the
residences  to the south (ST2), the noise from operations  would  comply with the City or
South Gate Daytime Noise Standard. At STI, ST2, and ST3, the future noise level from
Case I will exceed the Nighttime Noise Standard of 40 dBA.

For Case 2, the future noise level without noise control would be 55.5, 45.1, and 51.1 dBA
at the residences  to the north (STI),  south  (ST2),  northwest  (ST3),  respectively.  The
operations  noise at the nearest residential  receptors  to north (ST1 ) and northwest  (ST3)
would  exceed  the City of South  Gate  Daytime  Noise  Standard  of 50 dBA. At the
residences to the south (ST2), the noise from operations would comply with the City of
South Gate Daytime Noise Standard. Case 2 would only occur during the daytime.

Noise control suggestions have been identified  to reduce the noise leve(s to comply with
the City of South Gate Noise Standards.

Analysis, Section 6 discusses the Impact Assessment  and Section  7 presents  the Noise
Control Recommendations.  Section 8 discusses the Conclusion.

2.  NOISE

The magnitude  by which  noise  affects  its surrounding  environment  is measured  on a
logarithmic  scale in decibels  (dB).  Because  the human  ear is limited to hearing  a specific
range  of frequencies,  the A-weighted  filter system  is used to form  relevant  results.  A-
weighted  sound  levels  are  represented  as dBA.  Figure  3 shows  typical  A-weighted
exterior  and interior  noise levels that occur in human  environments.

Several  noise  metrics  have been developed  to evaluate  noise.  Leq  is the energy  average

noise level and corresponds  to a steady-state  sound  level that has the same  acoustical
energy  as the sum of all the time varying  noise events.  Lmax  is the maximum  noise level
measured  during  a sampling  period,  and  Lxx  are the  statistical  noise  levels  that  are

exceeded  xx-%  of the time of the measurement.  L50  is the average  noise  level that is
exceeded  50% of the time, 30 minutes  in a 60 minute  period.

The  City's  Code  limits  exterior  residential  noise  levels  to 50 and 40 dBA  during  the
daytime  and  nighttime,  respectively.  Additionally,  the  noise  standard  is 55 dBA  for

5.  NOISE ANALYSIS

AGI acoustical  data and advanced  acoustic  modeling  technologies  were used to evaluate
and assess  the Project's  operations  to determine  if noise  control  measures  will be
needed.  The CadnaA  Noise  Prediction  Model  was  used to estimate  the worst-case
operations  associated  with the project.  CadnaA  uses industry-accepted  propagation
algorithms  and user defined sound power based on ISO 9613-2 standards.  ISO 9613-2
is an internationally  recognized  standard  that establishes  a method  for calculating  the
attenuation  of noise from outdoor  propagation,  in order to predict the levels of noise at a
distance  from a variety  of sources.  The calculations  account  for classical  sound wave
divergence,  plus attenuation  factors  resulting  from air absorption,  basic ground  effects,
and barrier/structure  shielding.  Air absorption  was considered  to be under "standard  day"
conditions  of 59o F and 70% relative  humidity.  The site plans  and topography  were
inputted  into CadnaA  to establish  the x, y, and z site geometrics  for the analysis.  The
noise generated  by future operations  was calculated  by inputting  acoustical  sources  (AGI
in-house  acoustical  database  of children  playing,  live music,  background  music,  and
entertainment  areas calibrated  to number  of occupants)  as area sources  with constant
level of activity. Refer to previous  Figure 4 for the location of the analyzed  noise sensitive
receptors (STI through ST3).

9.  CONCLUSION

Acoustics Group, Inc., (AGI) was retainedto conduct a noise study for The Place @
Tweedy  Project in South Gate, CA. AGI has reviewed the City of South Gate Noise
Standards, conducted noise measurements,  analyzed the noise levels from future noise
sources at the site, assessed the impact of the future noise to determine compliance  with
the Exterior  Noise Standards,  and recommended  noise control  measures.

The Place @ Tweedy proposes an open-air Outdoor food hall with a central outdoor plaza
providing live entertainment. Two operating  cases were evacuated:  Case 1 (Typical
Operations Noise (without live entertainment  10AM to 11PM) and Case 2 (Typical
Operations  Noise with Live music entertainment  1 2PM to 9PM).

For Case 1, the future noise level without  noise control  would  be 55.4, 44.7, and 50.4 dBA
at the residences  to the north (STI ), south (ST2), and northwest  (ST3), respectively.  The
operations  noise at the nearest  residential  receptors  to north  (STI ) and northwest  (ST3)
would  exceed  the  City  of South  Gate  Daytime  Noise  Standard  of 50 dBA.  At the
residences  to the south  (ST2),  the noise from operations  would  comply  with the City of
South  Gate Daytime  Noise  Standard.  At ST1, ST2, and ST3, the future  noise  level from
Case 1 will exceed  the Nighttime  Noise Standard  of 40 dBA.

For Case 2, the future noise level without noise control would be 55.5, 45.1, and 51.1 dBA
at the residences to the north (STI), south (ST2), northwest (ST3), respectively.  The
operations noise at the nearest residential receptors to north (STI ) and northwest (ST3)
would exceed the City of South Gate Daytime Noise Standard of 50 dBA. At the
residences to the south (ST2), the noise from operations would comply with the City of
South Gate Daytime Noise Standard. Case 2 would only occur during the daytime.

Noise control suggestions have been identified  to reduce  the noise levels to comply  with
the City of South  Gate Noise Standards.

11.34.010  Purpose  and intent.

The purpose of this chapter is to establish  standards  and policies to control unnecessary,  excessive,  and

annoying  noise and vibrations  in the city of South Gate. It is the policy of the city to foster a quiet atmosphere  for

residential  neighborhoods,  and to implement  programs  aimed at reducing noise in all areas.

(Ord. 2323 § 1 Exh. A (part), 4-28-15)

11.34.020  Applicability  and exemptions.

A.  Applicability.  The provisions  of this chapter shall be applicable  to noise generated in any zone, subject to

the established  standards  and thresholds  herein.

B.  Exemptions.  The following  activities  shall be exempted  from the provisions  of this chapter:

  1.  Alerting people to danger or emergencies,  or sound related to the performance  of emergency  work.

  The South Gate Municipal Code is current through Ordinance 2024-04-CC,  passed Novemberl2,  2024.

  2.  Public  safety  or self-defense  warning  devices  or alert systems.

  3.  Public and private playground and school ground activities, including athletic and school entertainment
  events.

  4.  Bells,  chimes,  or carillons  while being used in conjunction  with religious  services.

(Ord. 2323 § 1 Exh. A (part),  4-28-15)

11.34.030  Nuisance  finding.

Certain noise levels and vibrations are detrimental to the public health, welfare, and safety, and are contrary  to

the public interest. Therefore, creating, maintaining, or causing, or allowing to be created, maintained, or caused,
any noise or vibration in excess of the noise control program of this chapter is a public nuisance  and shall be
punishable  as such.

(Ord. 2323 § 1 Exh. A (part),  4-28-15)

11.34.040  Terminology.

All terminology used in this chapter is defined in Chapter 11.60, Definitions. In all cases, terminology shall  have

the same meaning as defined by applicable publications of the American  National Standards  Institute  or its
successor  body.

(Ord. 2323 § 1 Exh. A (part),  4-28-15)

11.34.050  Program  review  responsibility

A.  Universal Enforcement. The purpose and intent of this chapter shall be upheld in all project and application
review, and decisions by all departments shall, to the fullest extent, be consistent with the regulations  in this

chapter. All departments shall cooperate with the noise control officer (NCO) to the fullest extent in compliance
with all federal,  state and local laws and regulations.

B.  Project Approval. All projects shall be reviewed for consistency with this chapter; the NCO shall  be
consulted prior to any project approval.

C.  Right of Review. The NCO has the right to review any project if nonconformance with this chapter  is a

possible consequence of a project's approval, and may request a department to review  and report on the

advisability of adding or modifying conditions of approval in order to mitigate or eliminate such nonconformance.

(Ord. 2323 § 1 Exh. A (part),  4-28-15)

D.  Measurementof Noise. All noise standards shall be based on the actual measuredambient noise level, as
measuredat the closest adjoiningproperty line betweenhabitableparcels or at the nearestpublic right-of-way.

E.  Unit of Measure. The unit of measure shall be designated as an A-weighted decibel (dBA), equivalent
continuoussound level ('-eq) standard. Noise shall be measured with a sound level meter that meets the
standardsof the American NationalStandards Institute (Section S1.4-1979, Type 1 or Type 2). A calibration
check shall be made of the instrument at the time any noise measure is made.

F.  Location of Measure.

  1.  Exterior Noise. Noise levels shall be measuredin decibels at the property line of the receptor property,
  and at least four feet above the ground and ten feet from the nearest structure or wall, where possible.

  2.  Interior Noise. Interior noise shall be measuredwithin the building or structure, and at least four feet
  from any wall, ceiling, or floor nearest the noise source.

(Ord. 2323 § 1 Exh. A (part), 4-28-15)

permit/variance  application  submittal.  No further action shall be taken where violations  are voluntarily  remedied
prior to or after written violation  notice.

  involvement is required to disperse the nuisance, the responsible party or parties shall be jointly and
  severally  liable for the following  costs incurred  by the city:

  i.  The actual cost to the city for law enforcement  services,  excluding  the initial response  provided by
  the NCO or police officer to abate any party noise violations.

  ii.  Damage to public property  resulting  from such law enforcement  response.

  iii.  Injuries to any NCO or law enforcement personnel involved in such law enforcement  response.

D.  Billing and Collection. The police department or NCO shall calculate all costs and shall advise the director
of finance. The responsible party or parties shall be billed by the director of finance following receipt of the total
cost. Payment shall be due and payable within fifteen days of the billing date. If the amount due is not paid, the
city may collect the debt, as well as any fees and costs incurred in its collection, pursuant to all applicable
provisions  of the law.

E.  General  Prohibition. Notwithstanding  any other provision  of this chapter or of this code, and in addition
thereto, it shall be unlawful for any person to willfully  make, generate or continue,  or cause to be made,

generated or continued, any loud noise from any source that unreasonably  disturbs  the peace and quiet of two or
more persons  of normal sensitiveness  who reside or work in the area.

  1.  The factors which shall be considered in determining  whether a violation  of the provisions  of this
  section exists shall include, but not be limited to, the following:

  i.  The volume of the noise;

11.34.110  Noise variance.

The owner or operator of a noise source that violates  any of the provisions  of this chapter  may file a variance
application,  consistent  with the procedures  of Chapter 11.51, Permits and Procedures.

A variance application shall detail the approved method of achieving maximum compliance  and a time schedule
for its accomplishment.  In its determinations,  the NCO shall consider the following:

  1.  The magnitude  of nuisance caused by the offensive  noise.

  2.  The uses of property within the area of impingement  by the noise.

  3.  The time factors  related to study, design, financing,  and construction  of remedial work.

  4.  The economic  factors  related to age and useful life of the equipment.

  5.  The general public interest, welfare,  and safety.

SUBJECT:  RESOLUTION  AMENDING  THE CITY'S  CONFLICT  OF INTEREST
CODE  FOR  DESIGNATED  CITY  PERSONNEL,  ADOPTING  BY REFERENCE
SECTION 18730 0F THE CALIFORNIA  CODE OF REGULATIONS

PURPOSE:  California Government Code F>87305.5 requires that each local agency adopt a
Conflict of Interest Code for designated City persoru'iel, adopting by reference Section 18730 of
the California  Code of Regulations.

RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  Adopt  a Resolution  amending the City's  Conflict  of Interest
Code.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  There is no fiscal impact from adopting a Resolution  to amend the City's
Conflict of Interest Code.

BACKGROUND:  The Political Reform Act, California Governrnent Code 6§ 81000, et seq.
(the "Act"), requires each state and local governrnent agency to adopt and promulgate a conflict
of interest code. The FPPC has adopted a regulation (2 California Code of Regulations § 18730),
that contains the terms of a standard conflict of interest code, which can be incorporated by
reference into the City's code. After public notice and hearing Section 18730 may be amended
by the Fair Political Practices Commission to conform to amendments to the Political Reform
Act. Therefore, the terms of 2 California  Code of Regulations  section 18730 and any
amendments to it duly adopted by the FPPC, if incorporated by reference in the City's code, also
become duly adopted to ensure compliance. The incorporation page, Regulation 18730, and the
Appendix attached to the proposed, amended Resolution, which designate positions and establish
disclosure categories, shall collectively constitute the Conflict of Interest Code (the "Code") of
the City  of South  Gate.

All officials and designated positions shall file their statements of economic interests, also
known as a Form 700, with the City Clerk as the City's Filing Official. If a statement is received
in signed paper format, the City Clerk shall obtain the original document and transmit it to the
FPPC or other agency as required upon request. If a statement is electronically filed using an
appropriate Fornn 700 e-filing system, the City Clerk will have access to those filings. The City
Clerk will make all retained statements available for public inspection and reproduction during
regular business hours (California  Governrnent  Code F>81008.)

  1

  108
 Currently,  the City  requires  a substantial  number  of employees  to fill  out the Fon'n  700 on an
annual  basis,  many  of whom  are not required  under  existing  California  law.  According  to the
FPPC, every elected official and public employee who makes or influences governmenta[
decisions  is required  to submit  a Statement  of Economic  Interest,  also known  as a Form  700. The
Fori'n  700  provides  transparency  and  ensures  accountability  in  two  ways:  (1)  It  provides
necessary  information  to the public  about  an official's  personal  financial  interests  to ensure  that
officials  are making  decisions  in the best interests  of the public  and not erihancing  their  personal
finances;  and (2) It  SERVES  as a reminder  to the public  official  of potential  conflicts  of interest  so
that the official  can abstain  from  making  or participating  in decisions  that are deemed  conflicts
of interest.

California  Governrnent  Code F> 87200 outlines  the  specific  provisions  concerning  who  shall
complete  Form  700s, of which  those positions  applicable  to the City  of South Gate are in bold:

  "This  article  is applicable  to elected  state officers,  judges  and commissioners  of
  courts  of  the judicial  branch  of  government,  members  of  the  Public  Utilities
  Commission,  members  of  the  State  Energy  Resources  Conservation  and
  Development  Commission,  members  of the Fair  Political  Practices  Commission,
  members  of the California  Coastal  Commission,  members  of the High-Speed  Rail
  Authority,  members  of  planning  commissions,  members  of  the  board  of
  supervisors,  district  attorneys,  county  counsels,  county  treasurers,  and  chief
  administrative  officers  of counties,  mayors,  city  managers,  city  attorneys,  city
  treasurers,  chief  administrative  officers  and members  of city  councils  of cities,
  and other  public  officials  who  manage  public  investments,  and to candidates
  for  any of these offices  at election."

California  Code of Regulations  Fp18700.3(b)(1)  provides,  in relevant  part:

  "(b)  for  purposes  of  Section  87200,  the  following  definitions  apply:  (1) "Other
  public  officials  who  manage  public  investments"  means:

  (A)Members  of  boards  and  commissions,  including  pension  and  retirement
  boards  or commissions,  or of committees  thereof,  who  exercise  responsibility
  for the management  of public  investments;

  (B) High-level  officers  and employees  of public  agencies  who  exercise  primary
  responsibility  for  the management  of public  investments,  such  as chief  or
  principal  investment  offers  or chief  financial  manager.  This  category  shall not
  include  officers  and employees  who work  under  the supervision  of the chief  or
  principal  investment  officers  or the chief  financial  manager;  and

  (C) Individual  who,  pursuant  to  a contract  with  a state  or  local  government
  agency,  performs  the same or substantially  all the same functions  that would
  otherwise  be  performed  by  the  public  officials  described  in  subdivision
  (bXlXB)."

Accordingly,  Section  18700.3(b)(1)  would  require  that  the City's  Director  of Administrative
Services,  who  functions  as the chief  financial  manager  for  the City,  would  qualify  under  the
category  of "other  public  officials  who  manage  public  investments,"  and, therefore,  be required
  2

  109
 to file  a Form  700.  Because  those  persons  who  work  in finance  for the City  work  under  the
supervision  of the Director  of Administrative  Services,  they would  not be required  to file a Fon'n
700. Additionally,  members  of the City's  Public  Finance  Authority  may  also be required  to file
Form  700s.

The  City  may  also designate  in its Conflict  of Interest  Code  any other  positions  who  shall  be
required  to  fill  out  a Form  700.  Pursuant  to  the  City's  Municipal  Code,  only  Title  1
(Administration  and  Personnel),  Chapter  1.52  (Municipal  Elections),  Section  1.52.081
(Electronic  Filing),  Subsection  (b) requires:  "Any  person  holding  a position  listed  in Gover'm'nent
Code Section  87200  or designated  in the city's  local  conflict  of interest  code adopted  pursuant  to
87300  shall  file  any  required  statement  of  economic  interest  reports  (Form  700)  online  or
electronically  with  the  city  clerk."  California  Governrnent  Code  Ep 87302(a)  details  how  to
identify  the designated  positions  that would  be required  to file  a Form  700: "Each  conflict  of
interest  code  shall  contain  the following  provisions:  (a) Specific  enumeration  of the positions
within  the  agency,  other  than  those  specified  in  Section  87200,  that  involve  the making  or
participating  of  decisions  which  may  foreseeably  have  a material  effect  on  any  financial
interest..."  Traditionally,  these positions  tend to include  department  heads  and, in some cities,
deputy  directors  and  other  high-level  managers.  Almost  universally,  these  positions  do not
include  mid-level  managers,  supervisors,  technicians,  and administrative  staff.

However,  the City  of South  Gate's  Conflict  of Interest  Code  requires  a substantial  number  of
mid-  and lower-level  employees  to file  Fortn  700s,  which  is not required  by California  law  or
prevailing  industry  standards.  These  additional  positions  currently  include:  Administrative
Services  Coordinator,  Associate  Engineer,  Assistant  Engineer,  Assistant  Plaru'ier,  Budget/Payroll
Analyst,  Building  Inspector,  Code  Enforcement  Officer,  Code  Enforcement  Supervisor,
Community  Development  Technician  II, Community  Development  Technician  III, Electrical  and
General  Maintenance  Superintendent,  Equipment  Maintenance  Superintendent,  Executive
Assistant  to Chief  of Police,  Executive  Assistant  to the City  Attorney,  Executive  Assistant  to the
City  Manager,  Grounds  Supervisor,  Housing  & Grants  Analyst,  Housing  Specialist,  Information
Systems  Administrator,  Infori'nation  Systems  Analyst,  Management  Analyst,  Park  Facility
Maintenance  Supervisor,  Police  Lieutenant,  Purchasing  Supervisor,  Recreation  Supervisor,
Revenue  Manager,  Senior  Accountant,  Senior  Administrative  Analyst,  Senior  Civil  Engineer,
Senior  Cornrnunity  Development  Technician,  Senior  Engineer,  Senior  Financial  Analyst,  Senior
Planner,  Street  and Sewer  Superintendent,  Technical  Services  Manager,  Training  Specialist,  and
Water  Division  Manager.

The City's  Conflict  of Interest  Code also requires  members  of certain  committees,  comi'nissions,
and boards  to file  a Form  700, which  is not required  under  the law:  Successor  Agency  to the
Community  Development  Commission  of the  City  of  South  Gate  Member,  Utility  Authority
Board  Member,  Public  Access  Corporation  Board  Member,  Parks  and Recreation  Commission
Member,  Civil  Service  Commission  Member,  Citizen's  Advisory  Cornrnittee  Member,  and
Cornrnission  for South  Gate Youth.

This  amendment  to the City's  Conflict  of Interest  Code,  last updated  on December  13, 2022
(Resolution  No. 2022-71-CC),  seeks to limit  the number  of persons  mandated  to file  Form  700s
to those required under California Government Code Fp87200, California Code of Regulations F>
18700.3(b%l), and a few additional high-level positions that may make or influence
governmental  decisions.  Specifically,  those  required  to file  Form  700s would  be limited  to the
following  individuals:

  3

  110
   A.  Required  under California  Government  Code F> 87200: Mayor  and City  Council
  Members, Planning Cornrnission  Members, Parks and Recreation Commissioners,  City
  Clerk, City Treasurer, City Manager, and City Attorney.

  B.  Designated  as "other  public  officials  who manage  public  investments,"  as outlined  by
  California Code of Regulations § 18700.3(b)(1):  Director  of Administrative  Services  and
  Board Members of the Public Finance Authority.

  C. Additional  Positions  as Designated  by the Conflict  of Interest Code:

  1.  Assistant  City  Manager,  Chief  of Police,  Director  of  Community  Development,
  Director  of Human  Resources,  Director  of Parks & Recreation,  Director  of Public
  Works, or any  other position  not  listed  but  later  designated  as an Executive
  Management-level  position.

  2.  Police Captain.

  3.  Building  Official,  Economic  Development  Manager,  Accounting  &  Finance
  Manager,  Budget  & Procurement  Manager,  Deputy  Director  of Human  Resources,
  Deputy  Director  of Parks & Recreation,  Deputy  Director  of Public  Works  - Field
  Operations,  Housing  Manager,  Parks  Superintendent,  Planning  Manager,  Risk
  Manager,  Transportation  and  CIP  Division  Manager,  Water  Resources  and
  Development  Division  Manager or any other position  not listed but later designated
  as a member  of the Division Management Association.

In accordance  with  the FPPC's  requirement  that there be a notice  of a 30-day  comment  period
before this item is brought to the City Council for approval, the City Clerk provided such notice
on Thursday, September 25, 2025, on the City's website and on the City's notice boards.

SUBJECT:  RESOLUTION  TO  AMEND  RESOLUTION  N0.  6377  (RULES  AND
REGULATIONS  FOR  THE  ADMINISTRATION  OF CIVIL  SERVICE  PROCEDURES),
ADOPTING  A  RESOLUTION  TO  APPROVE  THE  PERSONNEL  MANAGEMENT
RULES,  AND  TO REMOVE  THE  HIRING  RULES  FROM  A RESOLUTION  AND  MOVE
THEM  INTO  AN ADMINISTRATIVE  REGULATION

PURPOSE:  To amend  Resolution  No.  6377  (Rules  and Regulations  for the Administration  of
Civil  Service  Procedures),  to approve  Personnel  Management  Rules,  and to remove  thehiring  rules
from  a resolution  and move  them into an Administrative  Regulation.

RECOMMENDED  ACTION:  The City  Council  will  consider  an action  to:
  1.  Amending  Resolution  No.  6377  (Rules  and Regulations  for the Administration  of Civil
  Service  Procedures);
  2.  Approve  Personnel  Management  Rules;  and
  3.  Remove  the  Hiring  Rules  from  a resolution  and move  them  into  an Administrative
  Regulation.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  There  is no fiscal  impact.

BACKGROUND:  OnJune24,1997,theCityCouncilpassed,approved,andadoptedResolution
No. 6377 (A Resolution  of the City  Council  of the City  of South Gate Amending  and Restating  in
its Entirety  the "Rules  and Regulations  for the Administration  of the Civil  Service  Procedures"
(hereinafter  "Civil  Service  Rules").  The  purpose  of these  Civil  Service  Rules  was  to adopt,
implement  and administer  the recruitment  and employment  procedures,  under  which  employees
will  be accorded  fair and just treatment.

Attachment  "A"  to  Resolution  No.  6377,  which  is  titled,  "Rules  and  Regulations  for  the
Administration  of Civil  Service  Procedures,"  provides  for  these  rules  and procedures,  which
include,  but are not limited  to, the classification  plan, compensation  plan, examination  procedures,
recruitment  rules, disciplinary  procedures,  grievance  procedures,  nepotism  policy,  and others.  The
Civil  Service  Rules were intended  to provide  an objective  and fair approach  to how all employees
are treated;  however,  over the past 28 years since its implementation,  the rules have demonstrated
that  they  are ofttimes  too rigid,  that  some  rules  migrated  into  the employees'  Memoranda  of

  1

  116
 Understanding  (MOUs),  and that some rules have been made obsolete  by changes  in law,  such as
moving  away from  an "Affin'native  Action  Plan"  and towards  equal opportunity  employment.

While  the  Civil  Service  Rules  advanced  an  objective  approach  to  the  hiring  process,  it
unintentionally  yielded  difficulties  to the hiring  process  when  applied.  While  there  are several
examples  of  how  the  Civil  Service  Rules  hindered  the  City's  ability  to  effectively  recruit
employees,  the problem  was universally  recognized  by both management  and labor.  In an effort
to resolve  these  issues,  the City  met  with  all of its recognized  labor  associations  (Municipal
Employees'  Association  (MEA),  Professional  Mid-Management  Association  (PMMA),  Division
Management  Association  (DMA),  Police  Management  Association  (PMA),  and Police  Officers'
Association  (POA))  to create  a new Hiring  Policy  together  to which  everyone  agrees.  However,
because  these hiring  policies  will  be placed  into  an Administrative  Regulation,  they  need to be
removed  from  the  Resolution  for  the  Civil  Service  Rules.  The  amended  Resolution  for  the
Personnel  Management  Rules  is essentially  the Civil  Service  Rules  with  the hiring  protocols
removed  and some other  modernizing  updates.  The Personnel  Management  Rules  are attached
hereto  as Attachment  "A."

ANALYSIS:  In an effort  to make  the hiring  process  more  flexible,  efficient,  and effective,  the
City's  management  team met with  all of the employee  Associations  to come up with  a new set of
hiring  rules.  Staff  requests  that these hiring  rules  be removed  from  a resolution  and have them
placed  in an Administrative  Regulation  ("Hiring  Policy").  This  will  enable  the stakeholders  to
quickly  make  changes  and adjustments  to the current  rules through  the meet and confer  process.
Attached  hereto  as Exhibit  "B"  is Administrative  Regulation  336 ("Hiring  Policy"),  which  outlines
the changes  to the current  hiring  process.  Some of those updates  include,  but are not limited  to:

  *  Once the Department  of Human  Resources  ("HR")  has sorted  and ranked  all applications,
  the top  ten will  be the presumptive  list  of applicants  who  will  be interviewed  by  an
  independent  panel.  However,  prior  to the constitution  of that panel, the hiringmanager  may
  review  the top twenty  applications  and, if there  are nondiscriminatory  reasons  why  one
  placing  number  eleven  to twenty  should  replace  one placing  one through  ten, that change
  may occur to ensure the best candidates  are moving  forward  in the recruitment  process.
  *  Internal  and/or  promotional  recruitments  may  proceed  in  a closed  recruitment  (only
  employees  are permitted  to apply)  and may move  forward  as long as one applicant  has met
  the minimum  qualifications.  This  is to permit  the City  to promote  qualified  employees
  without  subjecting  them to the competitive  recruitment  process.
  *  The hiring  manager  will  receive  the top five  applications  for a vacant  position  (instead  of
  three);  however,  if the hiring manager has a nondiscriminatory reason why a particular
  candidate  is not a good fit for the position,  he/she may "non-select"  the candidate,
  effectively  removing  him/her  on the list.  This  will  permit  the hiring  manager  to move
  through  an eligibility  list,  fairly  consider  each candidate,  and exhaust  the list  instead  of
  waiting  for a year for the list to expire.
  *  By placing  these hiring  rules in an Administrative  Regulation,  it will  peri'nit  quick  changes
  through  the meet and confer  process  requiring  the approval  of the Personnel  Officer  and
  the employee  Associations.

 1.  PURPOSE  AND  SCOPE  OF PERSONNEL  MANAGEMENT  RULES

Pursuant  to the  City  of South  Gate  Municipal  Code,  Chapter  1.24,  these  Personnel
Management  Rules  are  promulgated  as  part  of  the  City's  civil  service  system  to
implement  and  administer  the  Civil  Service  Procedures  of  the  City,  under  which
employees  will  be  accorded  fair  and  equitable  treatment  in the  matters  that  herein
apply.  These  Personnel  Management  Rules  shall  apply  to those  persons  and  positions
within  the classified  service,  (as defined  in Subsection  14.9)  except  as otherwise  noted
herein.

  124
 2.  EQUAL  EMPLOYMENT  OPPORTUNITY

The City prohibits discrimination  against employees  or applicants for employment  on the
basis of race, color,  religion,  sex (including  pregnancy),  gender  identity, sexual
orientation,  national origin, ancestry, citizenship  status, age, marital status, physical or
mental disability, genetic information,  medical condition, or any other basis protected by
law. The City will afford equal employment  opportunity  to all qualified employees  and
applicants  as to all terms and conditions of employment,  including compensation,  hiring,
training, promotion,  transfer, discipline, and termination.

  125
  lO
 CLASSIFICATION  PLAN

3.1  Allocations.
  There  shall  be a classification  plan with  each  classification  having  its own
  title.  All positions  which  are essentially  similar  with  respect  to the nature  of
  the work  performed  and the basic  skills  required,  and are comparable  as
  to  difficulty  and  responsibility,  shall  be  allocated  to  a  common
  classification  for purposes  of pay,  recruitment,  examining,  training,  and
  personnel  administration.

  The  Classification  Plan  shall  be  approved  as  part  of  each  fiscal  year
  budget  and  listed  under  each  Department's  Authorized  Positions,  which
  may be amended  at any time through  City Council  action.

3.2  Maintenance.

  The  Personnel  Officer  shall  cause  to  be  prepared  a new  classification
  specification  whenever  there  is  not  available  a  currently  approved
  classification  specification  that  adequately  and  properly  describes  the
  duties  and responsibilities  of the position.  The  Classification  Plan  shall  be
  maintained  up to date  and those  classifications  no longer  in use  may  be
  abolished  by  the  City  Council  on  recommendation  of  the  Personnel
  Officer.  Positions,  the  duties  of which  have  been  changed  enough  to
  require  reclassification,  shall  be  allocated  to  a  more  appropriate
  classification,  whether  new  or existing,  in the  same  manner  as originally
  allocated.

  126
   COMPENSATION  PLAN

There  shall  be a compensation  plan for all classifications  of employment  with the City.

  4.I  Salary  Pay Table.
  The  Compensation  Plan  shall  be  set  forth  in  an  appropriate,
  comprehensive,  and  consolidated  salary  pay  table  adopted  by the  City
  Council.  Said  Compensation  Plan  shall  set forth  the.  (1) pay  categories;
  (2) classification  and the range  placement  for the classification;  (3) salary
  for the range;  or (4) flat rate of pay.

  4.2  New  Appointments.
  New  appointments  shall  be  at the  first  step  of the  appropriate  salary
  range.  In exceptional  cases,  and  in cases  of lateral  transfers,  the  City
  Manager  may  approve  appointment  at a second  or higher  step,  but not to
  exceed  the  highest  step  in the  salary  range  if the  candidate  voluntarily
  provides  documentation  to support  hiring  at any step  higher  than  the first
  step.

  4.3  Promotions.
  In case  of a promotion,  an employee  shall  be paid at that step  in the salary
  range  to which  he/she  is promoted  that  is closest  to and  equal  or higher
  than  an additional  5% of his/her  current  salary,  not to exceed  the  highest
  step  in  the  salary  range.  The  employee  shall  receive  a  new  salary
  anniversary  date  for  purposes  of advancement  through  the  steps  of the
  salary ranges.

  4.4  Demotions.
  In case  of demotion,  the  employee's  salary  must  not be in excess  of the
  highest  step  of the  salary  range  of the  classification  to which  he/she  is
  demoted.

  4.5  Supeivisory  Classifications.
  A person  employed  as or promoted  to a supervisory  classification  may  be
  employed  at one  step  higher  than  the  maximum  paid  to the  employees
  under  his/her  supervision,  provided,  however,  the  salary  may  not exceed
  the highest  step of the salary  range  assigned.

  4.6  Reclassification.
  The  reclassification  process  shall  be established  pursuant  to a policy  set
  forth  by the  Personnel  Officer.  In case  of a reclassification  of a position,
  the  employee  may  be advanced,  provided  he/she  meets  the  minimum
  qualifications  for  the  reclassified  position  and  complies  with  the  City
  established  policy  regarding  proper  reclassification  procedures.  Such
  employee  shall  be paid  at that  step  in the salary  range  to which  he/she  is

  127
  l?
   advanced that is closest to and equal or greater than an additional 5% of
  his/her current salary, not to exceed the highest step of the salary range.
  The employee shall receive a new salary anniversary date for purposes of
  advancement through the steps of the salary range.

4.7  Range Adjustments.

  In the case of a range adjustment, where a new salary range is assigned,
  the affected employee shall advance to that step in the new salary range
  that gives the employee a minimum of a 5% salary step increase, not to
  exceed the highest step in the salary range. The employee shall receive a
  new salary anniversary date. If the new salary range is lower, the affected
  employee's salary must not be in excess of the highest step of the new
  salary  range.

   EXAMINATION  PROCEDURES  FOR SAFETY  PERSONNEL

The following  procedures  are required  to be followed  in all cases  where  the position
sought  to be filled  is a SWORN  position.

  5.I  Lateral  Transfer  for  Police  Officer.
  Experienced  Police  Officers  from  other  California  law  enforcement
  agencies  may  be employed  by the  City  who  qualify  under  the  following
  terms  and conditions:

  5.1.1  Candidate  shall  possess  at  least  a  basic  P.O.S.T.  Certificate,
  hereinafter  referred  to  as "Lateral  l,"  or  be  eligible  for  a basic
  P.O.S.T.  Certificate  within  six (6) months  from  date  of employment,
  hereinafter  referred  to "Lateral  II."

  5.1.1.1  In cases  of Lateral  I applicants  the  City  Manager  may
  approve  appointment  in excess  of the minimum,  but in
  no  case,  in  excess  of  the  maximum.  Such
  recommendation  shall  be based  upon  the  applicant's
  training,  education  and experience.

  5.1.1.2  Lateral  II applicants  shall  start  at the  minimum  of the
  appropriate  salary  range  for Police  Officer.

  5.1.2  Candidate  shall  be  a graduate  or a P.O.S.T.  sanctioned  Police
  Academy.

  5.1.3  Candidate  shall  have  at least  six  (6)  months'  continuous  full-time
  paid  employment  of  a  P.O.S.T.  recognized  California  Law
  Enforcement  Agency.

  5.1.4  Candidate  shall  serve  and  successfully  pass  an  eighteen  (18)
  month  probationary  period.

  5.1.5  Candidate  shall  meet  all  requirements  as  age,  height,  weight,
  vision,  and other  items  of a physical  nature  as any other  candidate.

  5.1.6  Candidate  shall  successfully  qualify  in a background  investigation,
  an oral interview,  medical  examinations,  psychological  examination,
  and  any  other  examination  at  the  discretion  of  the  Personnel
  Officer.

  5.1.7  Candidate  shall  not be given  any credit  for any sick leave,  vacation,
  compensatory  time,  or other  time  earned  prior  to employment  by
  the City.

  129
   5.1.8  Candidate's  seniority  for any rights  or benefits  shall  be based  on his
  time with the City and not with any other  law enforcement  agency.

  5.1.9  Candidate  may  transfer  retirement  benefits  under  PERS,  however,
  the  City  of  South  Gate  shall  not  pay  any  additional  fee  to
  accomplish  such  transfer,  nor  does  the  City  recognize  any  other
  retirement  system.

  Candidates  who  are  not  currently  employed  by  a  California  Law
  Enforcement  Agency,  but are voluntarily  attending  a P.O.S.T.  sanctioned
  Basic  Police  Training  Academy,  who  qualify  under  the following  terms  and
  conditions,  may be employed  by the City:

  5.2.1  Candidate  shall  meet  all existing  Police  Officer  requirements  as to

6.1  Vacancies.
  Whenever  an appointing  authority  determines  a vacancy  to exist,  he shall
  request  a list of eligible  candidates  to the  position  from  the  Personnel
  Officer.  The  Personnel  Officer  shall  first  ascertain  that  a vacancy  exists
  and that  the position  is budgeted.  The vacancy  or vacancies  shall  first  be
  filled  from  the  lay-off  list following  the  order  in which  the  persons  are
  ranked  thereon.  Affer  the  lay-off  list is exhausted  or in the  event  there  is
  no lay-off  list for the  position  being  filled,  the  Personnel  Officer  shall  then
  certify  the  top  three  (3) candidates  utilizing  first  the  promotional  list,  the
  lateral  transfer  list,  the  Reserve  Police  Officer  applicant  list,  the  pre-
  service  applicant  list, and then  the open  or entry  level  list. One  additional
  candidate  shall  be added  for  each  additional  vacancy  being  filled.  The
  appointing  authority  shall  make  his appointment  of one from  the three  (3),
  or more  candidates  without  regard  to rank.

  from  the eligible  list.

  Appointments  to positions  on a regular  part-time  basis  need  not be made

  When  an  assignment  of duties  generally  requires  less  than  the  regular
  forty  (40)  hour  work  week,  individuals  may  be  appointed  as  hourly
  employees.  Such  appointments  shall  be at Step A of the salary  range  or at
  the designated  flat rate for the classification  and  shall  remain  such  for the
  period  of  appointment.  Vacation,  sick  leave,  holiday  pay,  retirement,
  uniform  allowance,  medical,  dental,  health  and  life  insurance  coverage
  shall  not be given.  Appointment  of hourly  personnel  shall  be from  existing
  eligible  lists if any candidates  are available.

  Employees'  Association  bargaining  unit.  Seniority  will  be  the  deciding
  factor  provided  that  ability,  special  skills,  job  performance  and attendance
  are  relatively  equal  and  satisfactory  when  filling  job  vacancies  in the
  bargaining  unit  through  reassignment,  transfer  or shift  change.  For  the
  purpose  of this Section,  such  vacancy  or assignment  shall  be a particular
  and  well-defined  job  within  a classification  which  is distinguished  by its
  geographical  location,  special  duties,  or special  and  unusual  shift which  is
  created  when  the  incumbent  has  been  permanently  removed.  Only
  employees  within  the classification  affected  by the vacancy  shall  be given

  present  assignment,  department,  or  shift)  on  the  basis  of  the  above
  seniority  and  other  qualifications.  Except  that  interdepartmental  transfers
  require  approval  of both  Department  Heads  or that  good  cause  be shown
  For denial  of employee  request.  This  Section  is to be applied  after  lay-off
  lists,  if any,  have  been  applied  but before  other  eligible  lists are applied.

  This  Section  shall  also  apply  to  acting  assignment  appointments,

 PROBATIONARY  PERIOD.

Any appointment  to a classified position From an eligible list shall be subject to a
probationary  period as outlined in the employees  MOU before an appointee  shall
acquire a permanent  civil service status in the position. An employee  may be
removed  by the appointing  authority at any time during the probationary  period
by submission  of a termination  notice to the Personnel Officer and the same shall
not be subject to review by the City Council. The name of such candidate  shall
not be again certified to the department  from which he/she was removed.  The
Personnel  Officer may restore any employee  so terminated  to the eligible list
from which he/she was removed  if there appears to be an adequate  basis for
anticipating  that the employee  might render  satisfactory  service  in another
department.  When a present employee  accepts a probationary  appointment  in a
new classification,  whether  or not promotional,  that employee  shall retain the
right to return to the position immediately  vacated. There shall be no permanent
appointment  to the position  vacated  until the reclassified  employee  has
completed  his probationary  period.

8.I  Employment  Requisite.
  Every  candidate  before  employment  shall  be required  to obtain  a medical
  examination  at City expense  from  a licensed  physician  designated  by the
  City.  The  certification  of  the  physician  shall  indicate  the  candidate's
  medical  condition  with  respect  to the work  he shall  be required  to perform.

  medical  requirements  for the position  shall  not be appointed.

8.2  Re-Evaluation/Fitness-for-Duty  Examination.
  The  Personnel  Officer  may  order  a medical  examination  of any  employee
  to  be  conducted  at  the  City's  expense.  The  examination  shall  be
  conducted  in order  to ascertain  the ability  of the employee  to perform  the
  normal  work  of his classification.  Employees,  who  in the  opinion  of the
  medical  examiner,  are medically  incapable  of performing  the normal  work
  requirements  of their  classification  may  be  assigned  to  a classification
  suitable  to their  medical  condition,  or separated  and placed  on a lay-off  list
  until  medically  qualified  to perform  the  duties  of any  positions  for which
  they  have  re-employment  rights,  provided  it is to the best interest  of the
  City and  in accordance  with  the Personnel  Management  Rules  governing
  the Civil Service  Procedures  of the City.

 13.  EMPLOYaMENT  OF RELATIVES

  13.I  RelatedbyBloodorMarriage.
  Relatives  of existing employees  will not be eligible for employment  with
  the City if potential supervision,  safety, security or morale problems  exist;
  or if potential conflicts of interest  exist.

  Relatives include an employee's  parents,  child, spouse,  brother,  sister,  in-
  laws and step relationships.

  13.2  Application  to Existing  Employees.
  Current City employees  who are related are exempt from this policy until a
  change  in job position  would cause a direct supervisory  relationship,
  would cause one family member to have access to confidential/personnel
  information,  or would  create the potential  for conflicts of interest  or
  problems related to supervision,  safety, security or morale.

  13.3  Marriage  Between  Employees.
  Should a City employee  marry another City employee,  the employees  will
  be permitted to continue to work for the City only if they do not work in a
  direct supervisory  relationship  with one another or if the situation does not
  create potential problems of safety, security, morale or conflicts of interest.

  If the  potential  problems  noted  above  exist, or if reasonable
  accommodations  cannot be made to eliminate the potential problems or to
  avoid  a direct  supervisory  relationship,  only one employee  will be
  permitted to remain with the City. The decision as to which employee  will
  remain in the City's employment  must be made by the two (2) employees
  within sixty (60) days of the marriage. If no decision has been made during
  this time, both employees  may be terminated.

  13.4  Application  to Elected  Officials.
  Subsection  13.1 shall not be applicable  to any person related by blood or
  marriage  to an elected or appointed  Mayor, City Council Member,  City
  Clerk or City Treasurer  of the City of South Gate who is employed  by the
  City as of the time of the election or appointment  of said official.

  HIRING  POLICY

The following hiring policy shall be applicable to Municipal Employees" Association (MEA) and Professional
Mid-Management  Association  (PMMA)  positions.  Executive  Management,  Division  Management
Association  (DMA), and hourly positions are not subject to this policy. Hiring policies related to sworn
peace officer positions  belonging to the Police Officers' Association (POA) or the Police Management
Association (PMA) shall be maintained  by the Police Department,  unless specifically provided for in this
policy.

1. Initiation  of Recruitment

Before initiating any recruitment,  the department  head may review the job classification specification for
the position to identify whether  updates are necessary. If updates are needed, the department  head will
collaborate  with  the  Human  Resources Department  to  propose  revisions.  The Human  Resources
Department  will review these proposals, ensure compliance with the City's practices and applicable laws,
and consult with the relevant labor association for approval. Once approved by the Personnel Officer and
the labor association, the revised job classification specification will become effective.

Prior to the recruitment  process, the department  head may identify which qualifications  (e.g., "desirable,"
"highly  desirable," or "preferred")  should be prioritized  during the application  screening process to rank
minimally qualified applicants based on departmental  needs. If no input is provided, the Human Resources
Department  will assign equal weight  to all qualifications,  following  established  practices and terms
outlined in this policy. No changes to selection criteria are permitted once the recruitment  process begins.

The department  head may also submit  any supplemental  questions  to be included  as part of the
application  process prior to the initiation of the recruitment.  Additional  questions for inclusion in written
or oral (panel interview)  examinations  may be submitted  at any time prior to the department  head or
designated manager reviewing any of the application  materials. The Human Resources Department  will
review these questions for compliance with laws, policies, and objectivity  standards. All questions must
be submitted  and approved by the deadlines indicated above, including recommendations  for additional
score weighhing. Modifications  to the questions  or their  weighting  are not allowed after the above-
indicated deadline has passed.

Recruitments  must be initiated as requisitions through the NEOGOV platform by the department  head or
a designated manager. Requests for recruitment  may also be made to establish  eligibility  lists in
anticipation of future vacancies.

As part of the initiation  process, the department  head or designated  manager  must recommend  a
recruitment timeline, specifying the duration of the recruitment  period and whether  early closure will
occur after reaching a specified number of applications.

  is currently
was contracted to provide constniction  management and inspection  services for a 100-working-

 Since then, the construction  contract  with  Sequel  Contractors  ("Sequel"),  Contract  No. 2025-30-
CC,  was  awarded  for  a longer  130-working-day  schedule,  with  work  expected  to finish  by
December  5, 2025.  To  keep  construction  management  services  in  line  with  this  schedule,
additional  time is needed  for TY Lin to continue  supporting  the project  through  completion.

Amendment  No. 1 adds two  more  months  of construction  management  and inspection  services:
one month  to cover  the extended  construction  period  and another  for project  close-out  activities.
This  extension  encompasses  the extra  work  requested  by the City,  weather-related  delays,  and
unforeseen  conditions  encountered  in the field.

Staff  recommend  approving  Amendment  No. 1 to Contract  No. 2025-03-CC  with  TY  Lin  in the
amount  of $112,537  to extend  services  through  January  31, 2026, ensuring  proper  completion  and
close-out  of the project.

BACKGROUND:  The  Fiscal  Year  2024/25  Capital  Improvement  Program  (CIP)  includes
funding  for  two  projects:  the  Citywide  Residential  Resurfacing,  Phase  IV,  and the  Citywide
Sidewalk  Improvements,  Phase X. These  projects  aim to repair  residential  street pavement  and
replace  damaged  sidewalks.  To  improve  efficiency,  staff  combined  both  projects  into  one
construction  effort  under  the Residential  Resurfacing  Project.  This  approach  allows  the City  to
complete  pavement  and sidewalk  repairs  at the same time,  minimize  disruption  to residents  and
motorists,  streamline  project  management,  and reduce  overall  costs through  a single,  combined
bid. The proposed  agreement  provides  for the construction  of both projects  together.

On January  14, 2025,  the City  Council  approved  an agreement  with  TY  Lin  for  construction
management  and inspection  services  in the amount  of $230,000,  based  on a 100-working-day
schedule.  Construction  began  on  May  27,  2025,  with  completion  originally  scheduled  for
December  5, 2025, totaling  130 working  days.

Subsequently,  on May  13, 2025,  the City  Council  awarded  Contract  No.  2025-30-CC  to Sequel
Contractors  in the amount  of $3,546,573  for the construction  of the project.  This  contract  also
established  a 130-working-day  schedule,  beginning  May  27, 2025, and ending  December  5, 2025.
A time extension  was later required  to address added project  scope, weather  delays,  and unforeseen
field  conditions.

Amendment  No. 1 extends  TY  Lin's  contract  to include  two  additional  months  of construction
management  and inspection  services,  adds the necessary  scope of work  to complete  the project,
and provides  one extra month  to support  project  close-out  activities.

  SUBJECT:  CHANGE  ORDER  N0.  4  TO  CONTRACT  N0.  2023-58-AC  WITH
  EXECUTIVE  MANAGEMENT  SECURITY  SERVICES.

  PURPOSE:  To extend  the contract  for  Executive  Management  Security  Services  to include
  services  through  June 30, 2026.

  RECOMMENDED  ACTION:  The City  Council  will  consider:
  a.  Approving  Change  Order  No.4  in the amount  of $80,000 to Contract  No.  2023-AC  with
  Executive  Management  Security  Services;  and
  b.  Authorizing  the Director  of Administrative  Services  to execute  Change  Order  No.  4 in a
  form  acceptable  to the City  Attorney.
  c.  Approve  the reappropriation  of $80,000  from  Salaries  (Acct  No.  100-401-61-5101)  to
  Professional  Services  (Acct  No. 100-401-61-6101)  to fund the change  order.

  FISCAL  IMPACT:  There  is no additional  fiscal  impact  to the General  Fund,  as all necessary
  funds  are already  included  within  the current  year budget.  The total  cost of Change  Order  No. 4
  is $80,000,  which  will  be covered  using  salary savings  from the vacant  Community  Service  Officer
  positions.  Staff  recommends  reappropriating  $80,000  from  the  Salaries  account  (100-401-61-
  5101) to the Professional  Services  account  (100-401-61-6101)  to properly  align  expenditures  with
  their  intended  use and ensure adequate  funding  for the contract  extension.  This budget  adjustment
  will  not place  additional  pressure  on the General  Fund.  Additionally,  the Police  Department  has
  submitted  a plan  for allocations  of funding  from  a Measure  A grant,  which  includes  $28,750  to
  offset  the cost of Change  Order  No. 4. Once the Measure  A grant allocation  plan is approved  and
  funds  are received,  the $28,750  will  be allocated  to reimburse  General  Fund.

  REPORT  SUMMARY:  At the recommendation  of the Director  of Parks and Recreation  and the
  Chief  of Police,  we are requesting  that the Park Ranger  program  be supplemented  with  the services
  of Executive  Management  Security,  Inc. fromNovember  2, 2025 through  June 30, 2026. The Parks
  and Recreation  Department  is still actively  recruiting  staff to fill  vacant positions  for the CSO/Park
  Ranger  Program  and have  a staffing  shortage  as we head into  the remainder  of the fiscal  year.

  Until  such time that these positions  are filled,  the Police  Department  has been deploying  resources,
  specifically  to the parks,  on an overtime  basis to ensure the safety  of the residents  and those who

  1

  176
 visit  our parks  and facilities.  The use of South  Gate Police  Officers  is exponentially  more  costly
than  that  of  Park  Rangers  and to help  reduce  the  overall  expense  of  park  security  we  are
recommending  the use of Executive  Management  Security  to enforce  park rules  and regulations
and conduct  homeless  outreach  to those who may be experiencing  housing  challenges.

Executive  Management  Security,  Inc was overseeing  security  at both the Urban  Orchard  Project
and the Hollydale  Community  Park Project  for the Public  Works  Department.  Additionally,  the
City  has previously  contracted  with  Executive  Management  Services  for the same services  being
sought  now  in 2023.  During  the course  of their  deployment  during  the 2023  season,  calls  for
service  at the park dropped  dramatically  and the response  from  the public  was positive.  Both  the
Police  Department  and the Parks & Recreation  Department  believe  that the results  will  be the same
for this period  of time while  we continue  to work  on hiring  additional  Park Ranger  staff.

  SUBJECT:  AGREEMENT  WITH  CJ  CONCRETE  CONSTRUCTION  TO  PROVIDE
  SIDEWALK  MAINTENANCE  SERVICES

  PURPOSE:  The purpose  of this item  is to approve  a maintenance  agreement  for the City's  first
  large-scale  sidewalk  maintenance  project  using  a new approach  of grinding  and ramping  uplifted
  sidewalks.  This  method  will  allow  more  locations  to  be addressed  under  a single  contract
  compared  to past efforts,  maximizing  the value  of the $1.1 Million  project  budget.  The project
  will  improve  safety,  reduce  trip hazards,  and lower  the City's  liability  exposure.

  RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City  Council  will  consider:
  a.  Approving  a Maintenance  Services  Agreement  with  CJ  Concrete  Construction,  for
  sidewalk  repair  services,  for an amount  not to exceed  $782,000;
  b.  Authorizing  the City  Manager  to approve  and execute  amendments  to the Professional
  Services  Agreement  up to a cumulative  amount  of $193,000;
  c.  Approving  a budget  amendment  to add funding  for part-time  Engineering  Aide  assistance
  and transfer  $125,000 in Gas Tax Funds from the Sidewalk  Maintenance  Services  budget
  to fully  fund the position,  which  is needed to provide  inspections  services;  and
  d. Authorizing  the  Mayor  to  execute  the  Agreement  in  a form  acceptable  to  the  City
  Attorney.

  FISCAL  IMPACT:  There  is no impact  to the General  Fund.  The Agreement  is in the amount  of
  $782,000  which  is budgeted  in the Fiscal  Year  2025/26  0perations  and Capital  Improvement
  Program  Budget,  as summarized  below.

  Sewice  Water  SBI  Gas Tax  Funds
  Maintenance  Agreement  $300,000  $300,000  $182,000  $782,000
  Contingency  -  $193,000  $193,000
  Management  & Inspection  $125,000  $125,000
  Total  Budget  $300,000  $300,000  $500,000  $1,100,000

  ANALYSIS:  The  City  issued  a Request  for  Proposals  (RFP)  for  Sidewalk  Maintenance
  Services  through  PlanetBids  and  received  four  (4)  proposals  from  qualified  maintenance
  contractors.  Following  a  comprehensive  evaluation  and  selection  process,  CJ  Concrete
  Construction,  Inc.  was  determined  to  be  the  highest-ranked  and  most  qualified  proposer.

  1  195
 Accordingly,  staff  recommend  awarding  a Maintenance  Services  Agreement  to  CJ Concrete
Construction,  Inc. in the amount  of $782,000.  This amount  includes  payment  of prevailing  wages
and is consistent  with  industry  standards  for comparable  maintenance  services.

Although  CJ Concrete  Construction  did  not  submit  the lowest  fee proposal,  the  City  is not
required  to award  this contract  based solely  on cost, as this procurement  was conducted  through
an RFP process  and is not subject  to the Public  Contract  Code's  low-bid  requirements.  The City
is proceeding  with  the most qualified  firm  based on demonstrated  experience,  qualifications,  and
overall  value.  In  addition,  their  first-year  fee  of  $255,500  is reasonable,  as it is below  the
$282,375  average  of all proposals  received.

In addition,  to efficiently  manage  the sidewalk  maintenance  program  while  reducing  costs,  staff
recommends  budgeting  a new  part-time  Engineering  Aide  position.  The  aide  would  provide
basic  field  oversight  of  contractor  work,  including  inspection,  documenting  quantities,
monitoring  compliance,  tracking  schedules,  reporting  field  conditions,  and maintaining  project
records  to ensure  the program  is delivered  as planned.  Funding  for this position  will  come  from
the project  budget.  City  Council  approval  is requested  to authorize  budgeting  this position  in the
amount  of $125,000  for 12 months  of service.  This  provides  4,432  hours  of service  at an hourly
rate of $31. Upon  completion  of construction  and project  closeout,  the position  will  be vacated.

BACKGROUND:  The  City  maintains  approximately  250  miles  of  sidewalks  throughout
residential,  commercial,  and industrial  areas.  Damage  is common,  most  often  caused  by root
intrusion  from  the  City's  extensive  tree  canopy.  While  City  crews  address  immediate  trip
hazards,  the backlog  of repairs  continues  to grow  each year,  exceeding  the Field  Operations
Division's  capacity.

To address this need, Public  Works  is implementing  a new strategy  that emphasize  grinding  and
ramping  rather  than  full  reconstruction.  This  cost-effective  approach  will  allow  far  more
locations  to be repaired  within  the same budget.  The  Council  is recommended  to award  this
contract  to begin  the first  phase of work.  Once complete,  staff will  use the results  to establish  a
routine  citywide  maintenance  cycle  that  reduces  the  backlog  and  keeps  sidewalks  safe  and
accessible.

The project  will  be located  citywide.  Construction  is anticipated  to begin  in November  of 2025
and be completed  in 12 months.

On June 16, 2025,  the City  issued  a Request  for Proposals  (RFP)  for sidewalk  repair  services.  By
July  17,  2025,  submission  deadline,  four  proposals  were  received  in the City  Clerk's  Office,
summarized  below:

 PURPOSE:  To approve  an Agreement  with  PermiTech  Solutions  Corporation  ("PernniTech")  to
 provide  wireless  consulting  services.

 RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:

  a.  Approve  Agreement  with  PermiTech  to provide  wireless  consulting  services;  and
  b.  Authorize  the Mayor  to execute  the Agreement  in a form  acceptable  to the City  Attorney.

 FISCAL  IMPACT:  The consultant  will  charge  $2,450.00  per application  reviewed.  For purposes
 of the  agreement,  the  total  amount  of  compensation  has been  set at a not-to-exceed  sum  of
 $50,000.00.  The exact amount  of applications  and fees to be billed  from  the consultant  is unknown
 at this  time.  Fees will  be paid  from  deposit  funds  received  from  telecommunication  companies
 proposing  to install  or modify  wireless  telecornrnunication  antennas  in the City.  These deposits  will
 create  a net-zero  impact  on the General  Fund,  meaning  that the pertnittee  will  pay at-cost  for all
 expenditures  deriving  from  the request.

 ANALYSIS:  The City  expects  to receive  and review  wireless  telecommunication  applications  with
 various  telecommunication  companies  (i.e.,  Verizon,  AT&T,  T-Mobile,  Crown  Castle,  Mobilitie,
 and others)  and desires  to engage  the specialized  services  of PermiTech  to provide  services,  as
 needed.

 BACKGROUND:  On July 27, 2021, the City  executed  ContractNo.  2021-96-CC  for an agreement
 with  Telecom  Law  Firm,  p.c. ("TLF")  to provide  specialized  legal  services  on wireless  and wired
 telecommunication  law  and  wireless  consulting  services.  In  September  2025,  City  staff  was
 informed  that  TLF's  legal  services  (legal  and  privileged)  will  be transferred  to  Colantuono,
 Highsmith  & Whatley  p.c. ("CHW"),  and wireless  consulting  services  had been  transfened  to
 PermiTech.  For  the  purpose  of  this  report,  the  focus  is on wireless  consulting  services  with
 PermiTech.
